newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile posts $1.2 billion trade deficit in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chile posts $1.2 billion trade deficit in 1996.

text.p: Surging imports and sagging copper prices combined to give Chile a $1.22 billion trade deficit last year, compared to a surplus of $1.38 billion in 1995, the Central Bank reported.
The trade shortfall was much higher than economists' forecasts of around $600 million to $800 million as recently as September.
Export earnings, affected by lower prices for copper and paper pulp, fell to $15.3 billion from $16.0 billion in 1995.
Imports, meanwhile, rose to $16.5 billion from $14.6 billion in 1995 as Chilean industry took advantage of a strong peso during much of the year to ship in foreign capital goods.
In figures released earlier Thursday, the bank also said December's trade deficit stood at $201 million on imports of $1.4 billion and exports of $1.2 billion.
